The '''2012 ICC Under-19 Cricket World Cup''' was a one-day cricket competition for sixteen international U-19 cricketing teams which was held in August 2012. This was the ninth time that the [[ICC Under-19 Cricket World Cup|tournament]] was held since its inception back in [[1988 Youth Cricket World Cup|1988]]. The tournament was held in Australia for the second time after previously hosting it in 1988 with the tournament being held across three cities ([[Brisbane]], [[Sunshine Coast, Queensland|Sunshine Coast]] and [[Townsville]]).

Six teams qualified from the [[2011 ICC Under-19 Cricket World Cup Qualifier|qualifying event]] as they joined the full members that automatically qualified through to the World Cup. The teams were separated into four groups of four with the top two teams qualifying through to the Super League while the bottom two will compete in the Plate Championship. After finishing second in their group, [[India national under-19 cricket team|India]] beat [[Australia national under-19 cricket team|Australia]] in the final by six wickets to win their third title after previously winning in [[2000 ICC Under-19 Cricket World Cup|2000]] and [[2008 ICC Under-19 Cricket World Cup|2008]].<ref>{{cite news|title=U-19 WC final: India win U-19 World Cup|url=http://www.hindustantimes.com/Cricket/CricketNews/U-19-WC-final-India-win-U-19-World-Cup/Article1-919521.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120826143816/http://www.hindustantimes.com/Cricket/CricketNews/U-19-WC-final-India-win-U-19-World-Cup/Article1-919521.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=26 August 2012|access-date=26 August 2012|newspaper=[[Hindustan Times]]|date=26 August 2012}}</ref> India's [[Unmukt Chand]] scored 111 [[Not out (cricket)|not out]], facing 130 balls and was awarded [[man of the match|Man of the Final]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Chakraborty|first=Amlan|title=Unmukt Chand leads India to third U-19 World Cup triumph|url=http://in.reuters.com/article/unmukt-chand-india-under19-world-cup-idINDEE87P03820120826|agency=Reuters|access-date=25 August 2012}}</ref> Australian captain [[Will Bosisto]] was awarded [[Man of the Series]].
Canada was originally scheduled to be the host of the event, after being selected as hosts in 2007.<ref>[https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/22925917/canada-host-2012-19-world-cup Canada to host 2012 Under-19 World Cup]</ref>

==Qualification==
{{main|2011 ICC Under-19 Cricket World Cup Qualifier}}
16 teams participated in the competition. The 10 nations with ICC Full Membership automatically qualified for the tournament. Ten further teams competed in the [[2011 ICC Under-19 Cricket World Cup Qualifier|qualifying event]] which was held in [[Ireland]] with only the top six teams qualifying through to the 2012 World Cup. [[Scotland national under-19 cricket team|Scotland]] (winners), [[Nepal national under-19 cricket team|Nepal]], [[Ireland national under-19 cricket team|Ireland]], [[Afghanistan national under-19 cricket team|Afghanistan]], [[Papua New Guinea national under-19 cricket team|Papua New Guinea]] and [[Namibia national under-19 cricket team|Namibia]] all finished in the top 6 to book their spot into the World Cup.
